troubleshooting.title: Troubleshoot the KC1 API
troubleshooting.shortdesc: What each error from the KC1 prediction API means, and how to fix the request. The API itself gave every response quoted here, on 19 November 2026.

steps-informal.p: The body leaves out one or more of the 21 metrics. The API lists each missing field in detail, by its name in loc.
Send all 21 fields, even when a value is 0. The API reference lists them.
The body has a field that isn’t one of the 21, such as a module name.
Remove the field. The API refuses extra fields so that it never ignores a misspelled metric without telling you.

remedy.title: 422 And “Input should be a valid number”

steps-informal.p: A value is text instead of a number, such as "loc": "many". Send numbers without quotes: "loc": 25.

remedy.title: 422 And “Input should be a valid dictionary”

steps-informal.p: The body isn’t a JSON object, often because the client sent a form. Send JSON, and set the header Content-Type: application/json. With curl, use -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @module.json.

remedy.title: 422 And “Input should be a finite number”

steps-informal.p: A value is too large to be a finite number, such as 1e999, or it’s NaN. The API reads 1e999 as infinity and refuses it.
Send finite numbers. Before version 1.0.1, the API answered 500 Internal Server Error to such a value instead of a 422.
/predict takes POST. A browser that opens the address sends GET. Use curl, a script, or Swagger UI at /docs.
The API stops at startup with FileNotFoundError and a path that ends in deployment_config.json. Nobody has trained the model yet, or ARTIFACT_DIR points to another folder.

Train the model with docker compose --profile train run --rm trainer, then start the API again with docker compose up -d. Outside Docker, set ARTIFACT_DIR to the folder that holds deployment_config.json and kc1_defect_pipeline.joblib.
Nothing answers on port 8000. Check that the API container is running with docker compose ps. The Compose file publishes the port on 127.0.0.1 only, so another computer can’t reach it, by design.
